The document says: "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH"

Context: HBM (Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH) was acquired by Spectris and in 2022-2023 merged/renamed. HBM became "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" — indeed, in 2021 Spectris combined HBM with Brüel & Kjær under HBK (Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer). The company renamed from "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" to "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH". The certificate was issued in 2022, so the certificate document shows the new name. The register holds the older/legacy name.

Is this "same-entity"? The rules say: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. This is more than spelling drift — it's a corporate renaming (Baldwin Messtechnik → Brüel & Kjaer). But it is genuinely the same legal entity that changed its name. Hmm.

The options: same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, unverifiable.

- same-entity: the value differences are cosmetic (spelling, suffix, accents). "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."
- different-entity: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Are "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" and "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" genuinely different companies? Legally, it's the same legal entity renamed (HBM renamed to HBK around 2022). But on a pure name-matching basis, these are different names. The rule says "Genuinely different company or person names" — the names are genuinely different strings, though they denote the same company over time.

The instruction's categories don't perfectly cover corporate renaming. But which is the safer decision for a fused record? Actually, is that right? Let me reconsider. "Same-entity" as a verdict means the two values refer to the same entity, and the difference is cosmetic. Here the values refer to the same real company (renamed), but the names are genuinely different words. Also, from a pure data-fusion standpoint without external knowledge of the HBM→HBK renaming, one cannot verify they're the same company; "unverifiable" is another candidate. Hmm.
